title: Free AI PowerPoint generator: slides from your notes · {name}
description: Turn your notes, a report or a spreadsheet into slides: a deck to present in the browser, or a PowerPoint file to change. Free, nothing to install.
h1: Turn your notes into slides, or a PowerPoint file.
lede: Give {name} your notes, a report or a spreadsheet, and say who the slides are for. You get a deck to page through and present full screen, right in the answer, or a PowerPoint file to change, its tables and charts included. Nothing to install.
try.ask: Five slides for Monday’s team meeting, from my notes: sales of {q1}, {q2} and {q3} in the first three quarters; two new clients this quarter; the website launch moved to November; next, we hire a second salesperson.
pane.ask: Five slides for Monday’s team meeting, from my notes.
pane.answer: Five slides, to page through or present full screen.

io.title: What goes in. What comes out.
io.why: Whatever you have: notes, a document, numbers. Say who the slides are for, and how many.
io.ins: Word or PDF, to boil down to its points
Excel or CSV, its numbers made into tables and charts
io.outs: To page through, present full screen, print, or share by link
Its text, tables and charts editable, with notes for the speaker
In PowerPoint, Keynote and Google Slides
The same points, to print or send
exact.title: Your figures, never made up.
exact.why: A slide is read fast and believed. Its numbers come from what you gave {name}, and when one must be worked out, a program does it.
exact.cards: Every figure on a slide comes from your notes or your files: {name} is told never to invent one.
A total, a growth or a chart’s values from a spreadsheet are calculated on a computer in a sandbox, in this tab. The first time, {name} asks before turning it on.
Each step shows as it runs. Open one to see what it was given and what came back.
where.title: Where your notes go.
where.why: There is no {name} server. What changes is the AI that answers, and you choose it.
where.cards: Your files and your tasks are kept in this browser, encrypted. Nothing reaches us.
Sent to the AI you chose
Your request and what you attach go to the AI you picked, and nowhere else. Under every answer, {name} says where it was done.
With the AI on this computer, nothing leaves it. It needs 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. No sign-up only with the AI on this computer.
No animations or transitions: each slide shows as it is.
It doesn’t use your company’s template: a deck has a look of its own, to change in PowerPoint.
Slides in the answer show no pictures. A PowerPoint file takes them from your own files only, never from the web.
A PowerPoint file is made on the computer in the sandbox, which fetches the tool that writes it once a visit: it needs the internet then.
{name} can be wrong. Check the slides as you would a colleague’s.
faq.items: Yes, with no account at {name}. The AI that answers may want one: {free} opens a free one, or use a plan you already pay for, or the AI on this computer, with no account at all.
Can I edit the slides in PowerPoint?
Ask for a PowerPoint file: its text, tables and charts are PowerPoint’s own, to change there, or in Keynote and Google Slides.
Can it make slides from a PDF or a Word document?
Yes. Drop the file in the box, and say who the slides are for and how many you want.
Yes. A deck in the answer pages through with buttons or the arrow keys, and fills the screen to present.
In a PowerPoint file, from your own files: drop them in with your notes. It doesn’t take pictures from the web.
Does it work in my language?
Yes: the slides are written in yours, right to left too, with numbers and dates as your language writes them.
end.title: Try it with the sample notes.
end.why: The request opens in {name} and is answered at once, or as soon as you choose an AI. Then try your own.
